note: Connections, geodesic actions, and tidal motion use the metric, proper time, and foundational free-fall concepts.
Curvature contractions and the gravitational action use the metric and its invariant volume structure.
Riemann curvature is defined through connections and covariant differentiation.
The cosmological term is constructed from the spacetime metric.
Matter motion and covariant conservation use four-velocity and covariant differentiation.
Einstein and Ricci curvature supply the geometric side and special forms of the field equations.
Weak metrics, clock rates, and light propagation use metric and causal geometry.
Classical trajectories and light bending follow from the geodesic equation.
Newtonian and post-Newtonian approximations derive from Einstein's field equations.
The Schwarzschild line element and horizon use metric conventions and causal structure.
Effective orbital dynamics derives from the geodesic equation.
Curvature invariants distinguish coordinate pathologies from physical singularities.
Relativistic particle quantities use invariant spacetime geometry and Lorentz transformations.
Relativistic actions and fields are formulated on Minkowski spacetime.
Particle and vector examples supply the first relativistic variables used by the variational formalism.
Covariant electromagnetic structures use events, the metric, and Lorentz transformations.
The Lorentz force couples the field to four-velocity and four-momentum.
Minimal coupling and the Lorentz force use the action formulation.
Noether and Euler-Lagrange machinery underpin conservation laws and Maxwell dynamics.
Maxwell equations waves and radiation use the electromagnetic field structures and interaction law.
